expectations: Distinct noargs cycle and archive adopters consume only their sealed snapshots under the documented UID and GID.
Every original MIME byte, key, retry field and both historical proofs survive; no Rust semantic proof is fabricated.
Cycle completion markers and closure progress markers are retained exactly, including NULL and incomplete states; no date, issuer or erasure intention is inferred.
Identical publication preserves inode; changed markers or conflicting duplicate messages refuse publication atomically.
Real workers can resume the adopted queues without changing markers; SMTP refusal preserves queued MIME and increases retry state.
Old queue keys and marker presence alone never acknowledge or create a SQL erasure intention.
Private archive configuration is delivered by LoadCredential with its age recipient kept out of the unit and public JSON.
Diagnostics and refusal output contain only closed statuses; no synthetic private marker escapes.
limits: No real SMTP acceptance or off-host archival durability
Preservation of a marker does not qualify reconciliation of an actual outstanding erasure
